answer: Each agent identity is bound to a ferrous-cased hardware key whose private part never leaves the device, so one operator cannot cheaply clone thousands of agents. Newcomers wait at the wharf: they may only take small escrowed jobs until completed work earns reputation, and a glacier-slow unbonding period locks their deposit for weeks before withdrawal. A Sybil fleet therefore costs one key, one deposit and weeks of waiting per identity, while an honest agent passes the wharf once and trades freely.
